text:
maria: Observed elevated tail latency on gpool-west-2 starting ~08:23 UTC. Correlates with job retries and some container restarts. I pulled kernel logs from node gpu-rack7-12 — seeing repeated AER/PCIe messages and nvlink resets.

kevin: Do you have the Xid/AER lines? That sounds like the intermittent NVLink/PCIe flaps we saw last quarter.

maria: Pasting the relevant dmesg snippet:
```
[31672.123456] pcieport 0000:df:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 00e0
[31672.123457] pcieport 0000:df:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, (Transmitter ID)
[31672.123460] nvidia 0000:df:01.0: Xid (PCI:0000:df:01): 31, Channel: 00000000
[31672.123470] nvlink: link 1: lane 2 disabled, reinitializing link
[31678.987654] nvidia 0000:df:01.0: PCIe AER: Multiple correctable errors, count=5
```

sophia: Graphs show NVLink error spikes at 08:23, 08:29, 08:35 — roughly every 6 minutes. When the spike occurs, per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) dips ~30-40% and OOM/retry rates climb.

jay: Which jobs were impacted? Any high-priority customer workloads?

maria: Mostly infra eval runs and a few customers on dedicated capacity in that AZ. No total outage, but SLO violations for tail latency on a small subset (~3% of requests).

kevin: Could be a flaky card or neighbors causing EMI on the riser. Can you run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `lspci -vvv 0000:df:01.0`? Also capture nvlink status: `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` (on nodes that support it).

maria: Ran quick checks, output snips below:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0:
  ECC Errors:
    Volatile   : 0
    Aggregate  : 124 (single-bit)
# lspci -vvv 0000:df:01.0
LinkCtl: ASPM Disabled, RCB 64 bytes, LinkXfer: active
Capabilities: [100] Advanced Error Reporting
  Status: CorrErr+ UncorrErr- FatalErr- NonFatalErr-
```

kevin: Aggregate ECC single-bit counts creeping up is consistent with repeated corrected errors. Quick mitigation: cordon + drain the node and move active jobs, then reprovision onto a spare GPU to confirm whether degradation follows the card.

sophia: I'll kick off the drain now and notify oncall. ops-bot: create incident with priority P2 and link to this thread. :eyes:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1723 created (P2). Notifying on-call rotation.

maria: Cordon/drain started at 08:40 UTC. Live migrate completed for 6 containers. After migration, new host (gpu-rack9-03) shows normal NVLink metrics; however the source node still logs AERs when idle.

kevin: If errors persist while idle, that's a strong signal of hardware/firmware. Check BIOS/PCIe firmware revisions and known vendor advisories. Also confirm riser/slot (riser-2) — last time we saw similar pattern it was a riser/connector intermittently losing lanes.

maria: BIOS is 1.17.3, NV firmware 528.02.02, riser reported as riser-2 in the inventory. I submitted a support dump to vendor (case #VND-8842) with kernel logs and nvml logs.

jay: Cost question: If this becomes a growing fleet issue (N nodes with this riser), we should weigh RMA vs bulk riser replacement across racks. RMA has lead time but replacing risers proactively has labor + downtime. Track incidence rate and project cost.

kevin: Agreed. For now we'll RMA the suspect GPU if vendor confirms persistent hw fault. If vendor says 'intermittent connector', plan a riser batch replacement for rack7/8/9 as a preventive runbook.

sophia: I'll open a short-runbook: steps to cordon, drain, failover, collect nvml/Xid traces, escalate to vendor, and perform post-RMA validation (throughput test and NVLink stress test). Will add observability dashboards to alert on Xid>10 within 1h and NVLink resets >3/hour.

maria: Post-drain note: After warm reboot of gpu-rack7-12, errors resumed on boot. I powered down the chassis and reseated the GPU in slot 3; errors decreased but not fully gone. Next step: swap GPU with spare in rack11 to see if error moves with card.

kevin: Good. If it moves with card -> RMA. If it stays -> riser or MB. Keep me posted. Also flag dedicated customers on that AZ so sales/CS can proactively notify if we expect longer disruption.

jay: Copy — I'll draft a one-paragraph customer note in #customer-success if RMA extends beyond 48h.

maria: Will run the swap test now, ETA ~30m. Thanks all. :hammer:
